answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each agent to a quarterly in-person credential at one monitored saffron grove. A passport office verifies a government ID and stores a biometric template, issuing exactly one non-transferable credential per natural person; a sybil cannot wander to another station to reuse the same template. Extra identities therefore need extra humans and extra visits. With per-period reward capped at R and visit-plus-issuance cost C, total profit for n sybils is n(R-C), positive only while R>C. Issuer collusion remains the weak point.
